summary: Democratic Gov. Gretchen Whitmer was term-limited, so the seat was open. Jocelyn Benson (Democrat) defeated John James (Republican).

candidates.name: Jocelyn Benson
candidates.bio: Jocelyn Benson is Michigan's Secretary of State. She ran with Winnie Brinks.

positions.summary: Says her central focus is making Michigan more affordable, including building more housing and making childcare free.
Says she would expand healthcare options in rural areas.
Says she will take Michigan's public schools to the top 10 in the nation.
Says she would take on the utility companies that raise rates.

candidates.name: John James
candidates.bio: John James is a U.S. Representative who was endorsed by President Trump. He ran with Jay DeBoyer.

positions.summary: Says he would phase out the state income tax over time and start with a one-quarter cut in income tax burden by recovering about $3 billion in waste.
Says he would use price transparency, direct primary care, telehealth, and rural provider recruitment to lower costs and expand access.
Says he would opt Michigan into the federal K-12 Education Freedom Tax Credit, expand charter school options, and make parental control of children's education the default.
Says he would repeal PA 235 and pursue an all-of-the-above energy strategy while holding utilities accountable on rates.

factCheckNote: Winner matches AP-sourced tally (MultiState governors tracker, updated Nov 4, 35 of 36 races called) Summary originally noted that figures reflected about 97% reporting.
